title: AI-Assisted Hackers Target Government Ministries and Critical Infrastructure in Latin America
content_md: Cybersecurity researchers have identified two active intrusion campaigns in Latin America that show how attackers are using artificial intelligence to work faster and solve technical problems. The campaigns targeted Mexican transportation services, government ministries, water utilities, and Brazil’s financial sector. The first campaign, tracked as CL-CRI-1131, affected organizations in Mexico and Ecuador . The attackers used “living-off-the-land” methods, meaning they relied mainly on legitimate Windows tools already installed on compromised systems. This approach helps criminals avoid detection because they do not always need to deploy obvious malware. During the attack, the group tried to steal highly sensitive information, including Windows Security Account Manager files and the Active Directory database file, NTDS.dit. These files can contain password hashes and other identity data. The attackers created shadow copies of drives and ran several numbered batch scripts to collect files. Their repeated failures and small changes to scripts suggested a trial-and-error process supported by large language models. Researchers also found that the attackers hosted NextChat, an open-source AI chat interface, on their own infrastructure. NextChat can connect users to different AI models, allowing operators to test prompts and compare answers.
